This shift suggests a broadened demand profile across semiconductor hardware suppliers as autonomous enterprise software capabilities expand.

Monolithic Power Systems's shares are extremely volatile and have had 34 moves greater than 5% over the last year. In that context, today's move indicates the market considers this news meaningful but not something that would fundamentally change its perception of the business.
The previous big move we wrote about was 8 days ago when the stock dropped 7.1% on the news that the chief executives of Anthropic, OpenAI, and SpaceX publicly united to call for a deliberate slowdown in the development of frontier AI models over escalating safety risks. According to CNBC, the sell-off was triggered by an essay published over the weekend by Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei, who urged a more cautious approach to frontier model advancement and called for independent safety monitoring. In a rare show of unity among competitors, the proposal was quickly endorsed by OpenAI CEO Sam Altman and SpaceX CEO Elon Musk. The unexpected warnings sparked immediate concern across the market regarding the sustainability of the heavy capital spending that has driven tech valuations higher. In response to the developments, Citigroup shifted to a neutral stance on broader equity risk, cautioning investors that any institutional pause or deceleration in AI deployments could temper corporate earnings growth and pressure chipmakers reliant on rapid, unchecked infrastructure expansion.

Knowles Expands RF Signal Chain Offering with New A-Series Attenuators
Wed, September 30, 2026 at 5:04 AM PDT 3 min read
New compact surface mount attenuators advance Knowles' strategy to provide customers with a more complete RF solution while delivering rugged, reliable performance from DC to 20 GHz.
ITASCA, Ill., Sept. 30, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Knowles Corporation (NYSE:KN), a leading manufacturer of specialty electronic components, including high-performance capacitors, radio frequency ("RF") filters, advanced medtech microphones, and balanced armature speakers, today announced the introduction of its new ATT A-Series Attenuators. The launch broadens Knowles' RF portfolio and the markets it can serve, advancing its strategy to become a one-stop source for high-performance RF components.
Utilizing precision thin-film technology, A-Series attenuators provide stable electrical performance and repeatable attenuation from DC to 20 GHz, making it ideal for densely populated and space-constrained designs.
Developed to address increasing demand for compact, rugged, and cost-effective attenuators, the ATT A-Series combines excellent attenuation accuracy, high power handling, and wideband performance in an industry-standard footprint. Utilizing precision thin-film technology, the A-Series provides stable electrical performance and repeatable attenuation from DC to 20 GHz, making it ideal for densely populated and space-constrained designs.
Attenuators are vital for aligning signal levels in multichannel systems, improving return loss, protecting sensitive components, and optimizing dynamic range throughout the RF signal path. As RF systems increase in bandwidth and operating frequency, designers need smaller, more precise components that maintain electrical accuracy and reliability in demanding environments.
"Our new A-Series attenuator product family fills a critical market gap by delivering broadband performance across DC-20GHz, high power handling, and excellent attenuation accuracy in a compact SMT package," said Robert Wagner, Vice President of RF and Microwave Products at Knowles. "Compared to many other attenuators currently available on the market, our A-Series offers a cost-effective solution with higher power handling, wider operating temperature range, MSL 1 rating, and ESD robustness."
The new A-Series attenuators utilize precision thin-film resistor technology on a ceramic substrate to deliver stable and reliable performance across frequency, temperature, and environmental extremes. The product family is well-suited for a wide range of applications including radar systems, electronically steered phased-array antennas (ESAs), electronic support measures (ESM) systems, transmit/receive (T/R) modules, wireless infrastructure (WI), satellite communications (SATCOM), and RF test and measurement (T&M).
Key features include:
Compact SMT package measuring only 0.080" × 0.065" × 0.012" (2.03 × 1.65 × 0.30 mm)
Standard attenuation values from 0 dB to 20 dB
Excellent attenuation flatness and accuracy
50Ω matched RF inputs and outputs for seamless integration into RF signal chains
Power handling rating up to 6.5 W CW at 100°C
Operating temperature range of -55°C to +125°C
The compact form factor and SMT-compatible footprint enable easy integration into space-constrained assemblies in demanding defense, aerospace, industrial and communications applications. Attenuators are vital for aligning signal levels in multichannel systems, improving return loss, protecting sensitive components, and optimizing dynamic range throughout the RF signal path. As RF systems increase in bandwidth and operating frequency, designers need smaller, more precise components that maintain electrical accuracy and reliability in demanding environments.

Tina Knowles may have plenty of life lessons to share with her grandchildren, but Beyoncé's kids have taught her a few things too. Beyoncé's 'blunt' kids give grandma Tina Knowles a life lesson or two and she's here for it

Beyonce's mom also shared a more personal part of her routine, saying she tries "to do something good for the world every day." According to Knowles, that mindset "resonates within me" and contributes to the way she feels.
Knowles also shared her favorite joke during the conversation, about an older couple who have been together for years. When the husband thanks his wife for always giving him space to calm down, he asks where she went. Her response? She had gone to the bathroom and "cleaned the toilet with your toothbrush."
"I love that," Knowles said, ending the conversation with her signature sense of humor and a reminder of the lessons she continues to learn from those closest to her.

"They're so innocent, and they're so free," Knowles said, adding that they taught her "to be free." She also shared her best hair tip: getting a trim every six to eight weeks. "You won't miss it. It will grow like crazy," she said. Knowles also revealed her favorite product from Cécred, the hair-care brand she co-founded with Beyoncé.
She picked the Reconstructor, calling it "magical" because it restores hair, makes it stronger, and adds shine. When asked about the secret to looking good at 72, Knowles pointed to taking care of herself. Her routine includes facials, exercise, and drinking plenty of water.
Beyonce's mom also shared a more personal part of her routine, saying she tries "to do something good for the world every day." According to Knowles, that mindset "resonates within me" and contributes to the way she feels.
Knowles also shared her favorite joke during the conversation, about an older couple who have been together for years. When the husband thanks his wife for always giving him space to calm down, he asks where she went. Her response? She had gone to the bathroom and "cleaned the toilet with your toothbrush."
"I love that," Knowles said, ending the conversation with her signature sense of humor and a reminder of the lessons she continues to learn from those closest to her.
